chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr and Fadala from Rifa'ah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had to fast two consecutive months, so he fasted one month and then fell ill. He said: 'God has bound him (with the obligation).' I said: 'A woman who had to fast two consecutive months, so she fasted and then broke her fast during her menstruation days.' He said: 'She makes them up.' I said: 'If she made them up and then despaired of menstruation (i.e., menopause)?' He said: 'She does not repeat them; that suffices for her.'
And from him (Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id) from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Asim ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a person who breaks their consecutive fasting due to illness or menstruation?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of al-Husayn ibn Sa'id and citing Imam al-Sadiq, clarifies the continuity of the expiation fast (kaffarat al-ghad) despite interruptions by illness or menstruation. It establishes that while the obligation to complete the two consecutive months remains binding ('God has bound him'), the specific days lost to natural biological states are excused and do not require repetition once the woman reaches menopause. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle that the 'consecutiveness' (ittisal) is preserved by resuming the fast immediately after the interruption, rather than restarting the count from zero.
